captions.instagram:
What is Le Chatelier's principle?

At equilibrium a reaction has not stopped: molecules still split and join, at matching rates. Squeeze, heat or feed a live box of molecules and watch Q walk back to K. Then run a Haber converter at 200 bar, open a fizzy bottle, climb to Leh with your haemoglobin, fur up a kettle and grow a stalactite.

→ Some reactions run both ways. Molecules split and join until the two rates match.
→ Squeeze it and the balance shifts to the side with fewer molecules. That is Le Chatelier’s principle.
→ Fertiliser starts as ammonia. Four gas molecules become two, so plants squeeze the gas to 200 bar.
→ Cool gives more ammonia but far too slowly. About 450 °C with an iron catalyst is the compromise.
→ A sealed fizzy drink is a balance: gas leaves the liquid as fast as it dives back in. Open it and the gas wins.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/equilibriumclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: What is Le Chatelier's principle? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
At equilibrium a reaction has not stopped: molecules still split and join, at matching rates. Squeeze, heat or feed a live box of molecules and watch Q walk back to K. Then run a Haber converter at 200 bar, open a fizzy bottle, climb to Leh with your haemoglobin, fur up a kettle and grow a stalactite.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/equilibriumclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/equilibriumclear

In this video:
• Both ways at once. N₂O₄ ⇌ 2NO₂ runs forwards and backwards together.
• Bread from air. N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ gives out heat and halves the number of molecules.
• Fizz and breath. A cola holds about 7 g/L of CO₂ under 4 bar; open it and Q leaps above K, so gas leaves.
• Scale and caves. CaCO₃ + CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ Ca²⁺ + 2HCO₃⁻.
• Where the rule slips. A catalyst speeds both directions equally and moves nothing.
